ca-alameda-2026-oakauditor-houston-micha.name: Michael C. Houston
ca-alameda-2026-oakauditor-houston-micha.bio: Oakland City Auditor; previously Oakland's Assistant City Auditor and a performance auditor for the City of San Jose's City Auditor's Office.

positions.stance: Will continue auditing City taxes to confirm they are used legally and as intended, and "relentlessly investigate allegations of fraud, waste, and abuse."
Will demand the City use data-driven performance and financial metrics so residents know how their tax dollars are spent.
Will engage residents and businesses to identify and audit areas that matter most to the public, like public safety and community services.

ca-contra-costa-2026-richmond-mayor-jime.name: Claudia Jiménez
ca-contra-costa-2026-richmond-mayor-jime.bio: Richmond City Councilmember elected from District 6 in 2020; formerly a licensed architect in Colombia who designed affordable housing.

positions.stance: Will split the $550 million Chevron settlement among growing the economy, helping residents share in growth, and quick visible neighborhood improvements, with resident input.
Will invest in port and industrial areas for clean businesses, fund paid job training leading to union careers, and simplify permitting for small businesses.
Will clean up trash and illegal dumping, fix sidewalks and roads, plant street trees, and keep improving parks, libraries and community centers.
Will keep funding the Office of Neighborhood Safety, grow the ROCK mental-health response team, and prioritize filling police vacancies with competitive pay.
Will clean up polluted land, build natural shoreline barriers against flooding, and add solar and backup batteries to fire stations, schools and community centers.

ca-contra-costa-2026-richmond-mayor-ande.name: Ahmad Anderson
ca-contra-costa-2026-richmond-mayor-ande.bio: Human resources director (Director of People & Culture, Gardens of Golden Gate Park) and former Chair of the Richmond Economic Development Commission.

positions.stance: Will pursue a strategy that holds people accountable while investing in prevention and support systems that make communities safer.
Wants a well-staffed police department with modern training and the highest ethical standards, plus community accountability and transparency.
Will expand mental health crisis response, fund violence prevention programs, create youth pathways, and address housing instability as a public safety issue.
Pledges to bring businesses and good jobs to Richmond, calling economic strength "the foundation of community stability."
Will cut red tape, improve access to resources, and make city government a partner for small and mid-sized businesses.

ca-orange-2026-anaheim-mayor-aitken-ashl.name: Ashleigh Aitken
ca-orange-2026-anaheim-mayor-aitken-ashl.bio: Mayor of Anaheim since 2022; attorney and former federal prosecutor.

positions.stance: Accelerating approval of mixed-use and affordable housing to expand access to affordable homes.
Deploying community policing, expanding mental health response teams, and upgrading emergency infrastructure citywide.
Supports new park projects, expanded youth programs, and revitalized community centers to serve every district.

ca-orange-2026-anaheim-mayor-rodriguez-a.name: Alfredo Rodriguez
ca-orange-2026-anaheim-mayor-rodriguez-a.bio: General Manager of a company that grew from an Anaheim-based operation into a statewide business.

positions.stance: "Safe neighborhoods, responsive policing, prevention, and measurable results."
"Public safety, coordinated services, accountability, and practical solutions."
"More attainable housing, predictable rules, and attention to displacement."
"Responsible budgets, transparent spending, and results for taxpayers."
"Simpler city processes, fair permitting, and a stronger local economy."

ca-orange-2026-anaheim-mayor-sharief-imr.name: Imran Sharief
ca-orange-2026-anaheim-mayor-sharief-imr.bio: Physician specializing in pulmonary, critical care, sleep and internal medicine; owner and medical director of HelpUSleep Center.

positions.stance: Will make public safety a top priority by supporting first responders and strengthening prevention and response efforts in every part of Anaheim.
Will focus on easing pressures on working families, expanding attainable housing, and protecting residents from unnecessary costs.
Will work to attract investment, support small businesses, and create good-paying jobs.
Will insist on transparency, fiscal responsibility and high ethical standards, and safeguard taxpayer dollars.
Will focus on clean streets, well-maintained parks, reliable infrastructure and responsive city services in every neighborhood.

ca-orange-2026-santa-ana-mayor-amezcua-v.name: Valerie Amezcua
ca-orange-2026-santa-ana-mayor-amezcua-v.bio: Mayor of Santa Ana since 2022, the city's first female mayor.

positions.stance: Supports outreach and engagement, expanded access to shelter and services, and "long-term solutions over temporary fixes."
Emphasizes collaboration between residents and law enforcement and "a balanced approach of accountability and prevention."
Supports small businesses and local entrepreneurs and encourages smart development and investment.
Advocates for infrastructure and transportation funding and supports housing solutions across the region.
Committed to strengthening school partnerships, expanding mentorship resources, and promoting safer environments for students.

ca-san-bernardino-2026-superintendent-va.name: Alejandro "Alex" Vara
ca-san-bernardino-2026-superintendent-va.bio: Educator with 34 years in education, including as a middle school principal and Redlands school board member.

positions.stance: Calls safety the precondition for learning; would audit every campus for deferred maintenance and publish counselor-to-student ratios annually.
Wants resources to follow need automatically for foster youth, homeless youth and students in poverty, with transparent equity budget reporting.
Supports career pathways by 7th grade, expanding technical programs countywide, and free college-application support at every high school.

ca-san-bernardino-2026-superintendent-bi.name: Cali Binks
ca-san-bernardino-2026-superintendent-bi.bio: School district superintendent for 17 years, including Yucaipa Calimesa Joint Unified; former teacher, principal and district administrator.

positions.stance: "We will support students by expanding opportunities for learning, well being, and college and career success."
"We will engage families as true partners in their children's learning."
Will empower educators and staff "with the resources, knowledge and tools needed to succeed."
"We will connect our communities to create limitless opportunities for every student."

ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-nuris.name: Thomas A. Nuris
ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-nuris.bio: Daly City attorney in general civil practice and chairman of the Daly City Planning Commission.

positions.stance: Wants a safe, clean environment with good schools, medical facilities, libraries, and recreation for kids and seniors high on the list of priorities.
Emphasizes economic development and growth of businesses and convenient, varied shopping venues.

ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-proan.name: Teresa Proaño
ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-proan.bio: Vice Mayor of Daly City, on the City Council since 2024; assistant to the president at Duggan's Serra Mortuary.

positions.stance: Will protect police and fire funding, recruit and keep first responders, and push for faster emergency response times.
Wants to fill storefront vacancies, cut permitting delays for small businesses, and grow local revenue "without raising taxes."
Supports affordable homes near transit and commercial corridors, meeting state housing requirements "on Daly City's terms."

ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-bayud.name: Tony Bayudan
ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-bayud.bio: Chief of Staff to San Mateo County Supervisor David Canepa for 10 years; vice chair of Daly City's Personnel Board.

positions.stance: Will improve housing affordability, expand access to healthcare resources, and help working families with the rising cost of living.
Will continue investing in police, firefighters and first responders so they have the tools and resources to protect communities.
Will advocate for a childcare center at City Hall to support working parents.

ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-daus-.name: Rod Daus-Magbual
ca-san-mateo-2026-dalycity-council-daus-.bio: Daly City Councilmember since 2018 and two-time mayor; tenured Ethnic Studies professor at Skyline College.

positions.stance: Says wages have not kept pace with housing prices and calls for collaborative approaches including all stakeholders to end displacement.
Will expand multilingual access, neighborhood outreach, and opportunities for working families, immigrants, youth and seniors to participate in local government.
Will support small businesses, good union jobs, fair wages, apprenticeships, and local hiring when public resources fund development.
Supports working with community organizations and regional bodies on environmental wellness and quality of life.
Public safety "must be rooted in care, prevention, and community connection"; supports mental-health resources and neighborhood-based solutions.
